_metadata.description: Identifiers, names and whole-food substances a person recorded by hand, because no ingested source carried them in a form a label would print. `entries` corrects substances a publisher already supplied and may never name an id that does not exist. `creates` adds the whole foods no register covers: every source in this corpus lists things somebody regulates, so palm oil and butter — printed on more labels than any additive — were invisible. Applied by curate.ts.

entries.why: The annex files two names in one field, so neither of them resolves on its own — and this is one of the six colours the EU requires a warning for.
EU labels print the E number, and the warning requirement is written in terms of it.

Banned as a food additive in the EU under its E number; food labels outside the EU still print it.
EFSA's re-evaluation and the EU authorisation are both written in terms of the E number.

The single most-scanned ingredient we hold, and no source calls it what every label calls it. Exact matching keeps 'lake salt' and 'Epsom salt' out on their own.
Labels print the refined and virgin forms by name.

The FDA revoked it for food in 2025, and labels outside the US print it as erythrosine or E127, neither of which resolved: an EU or Chinese label carrying it got no record at all. Not CI 45430: that is the cosmetic colour name, and the EU cosmetics annex already files it on its own entry.

creates.name: Palm oil
creates.why: On more labels than any additive in the corpus, and in no register, because nobody regulates it. Among the richest common sources of saturated fat.

creates.name: Palm kernel oil
creates.why: A different oil from palm oil, pressed from the seed rather than the fruit, and higher in saturated fat again. Labels frequently name both.

creates.why: Present on every chocolate label there is.
